claim: Skeletal muscle accounts for approximately 40% of adult human body weight.
source: Skeletal muscle accounts for approximately 40% of adult human body weight (Yin et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yin et al., 2013

claim: Muscle is responsible for 80–90% of postprandial insulin-stimulated glucose uptake.
source: muscle is also a key metabolic organ, responsible for 80–90% of postprandial insulin-stimulated glucose uptake.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge in the field

claim: Satellite cells are indispensable for postnatal muscle growth and regeneration.
source: In adult skeletal muscles, resident stem cells called satellite cells (SCs) are indispensable for postnatal muscle growth and regeneration (Le Grand and Rudnicki, 2007; Lepper et al., 2011; Murphy et al., 2011; Pawlikowski et al., 2015; Relaix and Zammit, 2012; Sambasivan et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: Satellite cells are wedged between the plasma membrane of muscle fiber and the basal lamina that surrounds the myofiber.
source: SCs are wedged between the plasma membrane of muscle fiber (i.e., myofiber) and the basal lamina that surrounds the myofiber.
evidence: Stated as established anatomical knowledge

claim: Age-related muscle wasting (sarcopenia) and degenerative muscular dystrophy are linked to decline of SCs' abundance and functionality.
source: Age-related muscle wasting (sarcopenia) and degenerative muscular dystrophy are linked to decline of SCs' abundance and functionality, as a result of changes in niche function and intrinsic properties of SCs (Conboy et al., 2005; Sacco and Puri, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Conboy et al., 2005 and Sacco and Puri, 2015

claim: Pax7 is the faithful marker for SCs and is indispensable for proper postnatal muscle regeneration.
source: Among them, Pax7 (Paired box 7) is the faithful marker for SCs, and also indispensable for proper postnatal muscle regeneration by controlling expansion and differentiation of SCs (Kuang et al., 2006; Seale et al., 2000; von Maltzahn et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: When stimulated, SCs break quiescence and express MyoD, which promotes S-phase entry and facilitates SCs activation.
source: When stimulated, SCs break quiescence and express MyoD, which promotes S-phase entry and facilitates SCs activation (Halevy et al., 2004; Olguin and Olwin, 2004; Zammit et al., 2004; Zhang et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: In zebrafish and amphibians, dedifferentiation is an integral part of tissue regeneration.
source: In zebrafish and amphibians, dedifferentiation is an integral part of tissue regeneration (Jopling et al., 2010; Morrison et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to Jopling et al., 2010 and Morrison et al., 2006

claim: In the newt, fragmentation and dedifferentiation of myofibers generate a pool of proliferating mononucleated cells that give rise to the skeletal muscle of a new limb.
source: Specifically, in the newt, fragmentation and dedifferentiation of myofibers generate a pool of proliferating mononucleated cells that give rise to the skeletal muscle of a new limb (Sandoval-Guzman et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sandoval-Guzman et al., 2014

claim: In mammals, there is no evidence of dedifferentiation that occurs as a natural part of tissue regeneration.
source: However, in mammals, there is no evidence of dedifferentiation that occurs as a natural part of tissue regeneration.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge in the field

claim: Concomitant inactivation of two tumor-suppressors Arf and Rb in mononucleated mouse myocytes led to loss of differentiation properties, cell cycle reentry and generation of cells that were capable to redifferentiate into skeletal muscles.
source: For instance, concomitant inactivation of two tumor-suppressors Arf and Rb in mononucleated mouse myocytes led to loss of differentiation properties, cell cycle reentry and generation of cells that were capable to redifferentiate into skeletal muscles (Pajcini et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Pajcini et al., 2010

claim: Notch signaling is indispensable for maintaining quiescence and self-renewal of SCs.
source: In postnatal myogenesis, Notch signaling is indispensable for maintaining quiescence and self-renewal of SCs (Bjornson et al., 2012; Fukada et al., 2011; Mourikis et al., 2012b; Vasyutina et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: During development SCs rely on Notch signaling to acquire 'satellite' position aside of myofiber by controlling the assembly of basal lamina.
source: In addition, during development SCs rely on Notch signaling to acquire 'satellite' position aside of myofiber by controlling the assembly of basal lamina (Brohl et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Brohl et al., 2012

claim: Notch is a potent inhibitor of muscle differentiation by inhibiting expression of MyoD.
source: Furthermore, Notch is a potent inhibitor of muscle differentiation by inhibiting expression of MyoD (Delfini et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Delfini et al., 2000

claim: Deletion of Rbpj or Dll1 led to premature differentiation and depletion of SCs, thus a loss of muscle growth and severe muscle hypotrophy.
source: As such, deletion of Rbpj or Dll1 led to premature differentiation and depletion of SCs, thus a loss of muscle growth and severe muscle hypotrophy (Schuster-Gossler et al., 2007; Vasyutina et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to Schuster-Gossler et al., 2007 and Vasyutina et al., 2007

claim: None of the freshly isolated SCs from MLC-Td and MCK-Td mice expressed RFP.
source: First, we cultured myoblasts from 1-month old MLC-Td and MCK-Td mice, and found that none of the freshly isolated SCs expressed RFP.
evidence: Based on experimental observation in cultured cells

claim: RFP expression was first detected in a few MLC-Td but not MCK-Td myocytes that were Pax7–, MyoD–, MyoG–, but MF20+ under growth conditions.
source: Under growth conditions, RFP expression was first detected in a few MLC-Td but not MCK-Td myocytes that were Pax7–, MyoD–, MyoG–, but MF20+ (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: RFP was readily detectable in fusion-competent MLC-Td myocytes immediately after switching to the differentiation medium.
source: Later on, RFP was readily detectable in fusion-competent MLC-Td myocytes immediately after switching to the differentiation medium (Figure 1B).
evidence: Based on experimental observation shown in Figure 1B

claim: RFP was only detected in post-fusion myotubes starting from day-3 after induction of myogenic differentiation in MCK-Td cells.
source: By contrast, RFP was only detected in post-fusion myotubes starting from day-3 after induction of myogenic differentiation in MCK-Td cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: Based on experimental observation shown in Figure 1B

claim: 96% and 55% myonuclei were nG+ in cross sections of tibialis anterior (TA) muscles from postnatal day-12 MLC-nTnG and MCK-nTnG mice, respectively.
source: Intriguingly, 96% and 55% myonuclei (within myofibers outlined by dystrophin) were nG+ in cross sections of tibialis anterior (TA) muscles from postnatal day-12 MLC-nTnG and MCK-nTnG mice, respectively (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: Based on quantification data shown in Figure 1C and D

claim: By 1.5-month old, all myonuclei (100%) became nG+ in both MLC-nTnG and MCK-nTnG mice.
source: By 1.5-month old, all myonuclei (100%) became nG+ in both MLC-nTnG and MCK-nTnG mice (data not shown), coinciding with the completion of the myonuclei addition in growing muscles (White et al., 2010).
evidence: Based on experimental observation and citation to White et al., 2010

claim: Massive nG+ myonuclei were detected 4 days post injury (dpi) in MLC-nTnG mice.
source: Consistently, we detected massive nG+ myonuclei 4 days post injury (dpi) in MLC-nTnG mice (Figure 1E1).
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1E1

claim: MCK-nTnG myofibers didn't express nG at 4 dpi but started to express nG at 6 dpi, and peaked at 9 dpi.
source: By contrast, MCK-nTnG myofibers didn't express nG at 4 dpi (Figure 1E2), but started to express nG at 6 dpi (Figure 1E3), and peaked at 9 dpi (Figure 1E4).
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1E2-E4

claim: Myonuclei in both MCK-nTnG and MLC-nTnG muscles were predominantly nG+ at 21 dpi, which marks the completion of muscle regeneration.
source: Eventually, myonuclei in both MCK-nTnG and MLC-nTnG muscles were predominantly nG+ at 21 dpi (Figure 1E5 and E6), which marks the completion of muscle regeneration.
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1E5 and E6

claim: MLC-Cre activation is detected earliest in mononuclear myocytes and MCK-Cre is detected only in multinucleated myotubes (myofibers).
source: In summary, these in vitro and in vivo genetic mapping results reveal sequential activation of MLC-Cre and MCK-Cre along myogenesis, with earliest MLC-Cre activation detected in mononuclear myocytes and MCK-Cre detected only in multinucleated myotubes (myofibers).
evidence: Based on the combined in vitro and in vivo experimental data presented

claim: MLC-N1ICD mice were born at an expected Mendelian ratio with normal body weight.
source: The MLC-N1ICD mice were born at an expected Mendelian ratio with normal body weight (data not shown).
evidence: Based on experimental observation

claim: Adult MLC-N1ICD mice expressed higher levels of Notch1ICD and its target genes, including Hes1, Hey1 and Heyl, in both fast and slow muscles.
source: Adult MLC-N1ICD mice expressed higher levels of Notch1ICD and its target genes, including Hes1, Hey1 and Heyl, in both fast (gastroceminus, Figure 2B) and slow (soleus, Figure 2C) muscles, confirming activation of Notch signaling.
evidence: Based on gene expression data shown in Figure 2B and 2C

claim: MLC-N1ICD mice showed less body weights at weaning (postnatal day-21), and less body weight gains and muscle mass in adulthood, compared with wildtype (WT) mice.
source: However, MLC-N1ICD mice showed less body weights at weaning (postnatal day-21), and less body weight gains and muscle mass in adulthood, compared with wildtype (WT) mice (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: Based on body weight and muscle mass measurements shown in Figure 2D and E

claim: By 4-month of age, all MLC-N1ICD mice displayed prominent kyphosis.
source: By 4-month of age, all MLC-N1ICD mice displayed prominent kyphosis (Figure 2F), which is a sign of severe muscle weakness and a hallmark of aging.
evidence: Based on phenotypic observation shown in Figure 2F

claim: MLC-N1ICD mice had only around half the myonuclei numbers of WT myofibers.
source: As early phase of postnatal muscle growth is normally mediated by myonuclei addition, we quantified the myonucleus numbers of EDL myofibers, and found that MLC-N1ICD had only around half the myonuclei numbers of WT myofibers (Figure 2G and H).
evidence: Based on myonucleus counting data shown in Figure 2G and H

claim: MLC-N1ICD mice were subjected to premature death starting from 2-month of age, and no MLC-N1ICD mice survived longer than 6 months.
source: Consequently, MLC-N1ICD mice were subjected to premature death starting from 2-month of age, and no MLC-N1ICD mice survived longer than 6 months (Figure 2I).
evidence: Based on survival curve data shown in Figure 2I

claim: MLC-N1ICD mice ran significantly more slowly and shorter distance compared with WT mice.
source: Notably, MLC-N1ICD mice ran significantly more slowly and shorter distance compared with WT mice (Figure 2J).
evidence: Based on treadmill exercise test data shown in Figure 2J

claim: MLC-N1ICD mice showed lower gripping strength.
source: In addition, MLC-N1ICD mice showed lower gripping strength (Figure 2K).
evidence: Based on gripping strength measurement shown in Figure 2K

claim: MLC-N1ICD mice showed drastically compromised muscle regeneration at 7 dpi after CTX injection.
source: In non-CTX injected leg, the MLC-N1ICD myofibers are smaller than those of WT mice (Figure 3A, left; Figure 2G); with CTX injection, MLC-N1ICD showed drastically compromised muscle regeneration, evidenced by massive infiltration of non-muscle cells into TA (Figure 3A; right).
evidence: Based on H&E staining shown in Figure 3A

claim: MLC-N1ICD muscles showed greatly increased number of Pax7+ satellite cells, in both control and injured TA muscles.
source: Unexpectedly, despite of severe regenerative defects, MLC-N1ICD muscles showed greatly increased number of Pax7+ satellite cells, in both control and injured TA muscles (Figure 3B).
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3B

claim: MLC-N1ICD EDL myofibers showed 10-times more Pax7+ satellite cells than WT myofibers.
source: Similarly, MLC-N1ICD EDL myofibers showed 10-times more Pax7+ satellite cells than WT myofibers (Figure 3C).
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence and quantification data shown in Figure 3C

claim: Pax7 expression was significantly higher at both mRNA and protein levels in MLC-N1ICD muscles.
source: Consistently, Pax7 expression was significantly higher at both mRNA and protein levels in MLC-N1ICD muscles (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: Based on Western blot and gene expression data shown in Figure 3D and E

claim: None of the Pax7+ cells in MLC-N1ICD mice expressed Ki67.
source: To determine whether these changes are caused by SC proliferation, we co-labeled MLC-N1ICD SCs with Ki67. However, none of the Pax7+ cells expressed Ki67 (Figure 3F).
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3F

claim: Pax7+ cells in MLC-N1ICD mice did not express MyoD and MyoG.
source: Similarly, we didn't detect MyoD and MyoG expression in these cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A

claim: MLC-N1ICD muscles expressed significantly higher levels of quiescent SC marker genes (Cdh15, Calcr, Tenm4).
source: Indeed, we detected significantly higher expression levels of marker genes that are abundantly (Cdh15, encodes M-cadherin) or exclusively (calcitonin receptor, Calcr; teneurin transmembrane protein 4, Tenm4) expressed by quiescent SCs (Figure 3G) (Fukada et al., 2007).
evidence: Based on gene expression data shown in Figure 3G and citation to Fukada et al., 2007

claim: 73% of the Pax7+ SCs in MLC-N1ICD mice were labeled as Td+, demonstrating that they were previously differentiated (Myl1+).
source: Strikingly, 73% of the Pax7+ SCs in MLC-N1ICD mice were labeled as Td+ (Figure 3H; second row), demonstrating that they were previously differentiated (Myl1+).
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3H

claim: No Pax7+/Td+ SC was detected in resting and CTX-injected muscles of adult MLC-Td mice.
source: As a control, no Pax7+/Td+ SC was detected in resting and CTX-injected muscles of adult MLC-Td mice (Figure 3 H; first row, Figure 3—figure supplement 1D), which is consistent with the earlier tracing result of cultured MLC-Td SCs (Figure 1A).
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3H and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D

claim: Notch1 activation dedifferentiated MLC-Cre+ myocytes into quiescent SCs.
source: In summary, Notch1 activation dedifferentiated MLC-Cre+ myocytes into quiescent SCs.
evidence: Based on the combined experimental data showing Pax7+/Td+ cells in MLC-N1ICD mice

claim: MCK-N1ICD mice were born at normal Mendelian ratio and expressed higher levels of Notch1 and Notch target genes, including Hes1, Hes5, Hey1 and Heyl.
source: MCK-N1ICD mice were born at normal Mendelian ratio and expressed higher levels of Notch1 and Notch target genes, including Hes1, Hes5, Hey1 and Heyl (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Based on gene expression data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A

claim: Adult MCK-N1ICD mice didn't show any significant differences in body weight, myosin expression, neuromuscular junction morphology, denervation responses, exercise performance and gripping strength compared to WT littermates.
source: Compared to WT littermates, adult MCK-N1ICD mice didn't show any significant differences in body weight, myosin expression, neuromuscular junction morphology, denervation responses, exercise performance and gripping strength (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B–H).
evidence: Based on multiple experimental measurements shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B–H

claim: Adult MCK-N1ICD mice displayed normal muscle regeneration after a single episode of CTX injury.
source: In addition, adult MCK-N1ICD mice displayed normal muscle regeneration after a single episode of CTX injury (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A; first row).
evidence: Based on H&E staining shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A

claim: In response to multiple rounds of injuries induced by repetitive CTX injections, the MCK-N1ICD muscles regenerated much better than the WT muscles.
source: In response to multiple rounds of injuries induced by repetitive CTX injections, however, the MCK-N1ICD muscles regenerated much better than the WT muscles, manifested by overall larger muscle volume (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B), appearance of larger regenerating myofibers and homogeneous regenerated area throughout the muscle (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A; second row).
evidence: Based on H&E staining and muscle images shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and 2B

claim: Aged muscles (>1-year old) expressed reduced levels of Notch receptors and Notch targets than young muscles (around 1 month old).
source: As aged muscles (>1-year old) expressed reduced levels of Notch receptors and Notch targets than young muscles (around 1 month old) (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C and D), we investigated if MCK-N1ICD improves muscle regeneration in aged mice.
evidence: Based on gene expression data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C and D

claim: At 15-month old, MCK-N1ICD muscles regenerated more efficiently than those of WT littermates, evidenced by larger and more regenerating myofibers, reduced adipocyte infiltration.
source: At 15-month old, MCK-N1ICD muscles regenerated more efficiently than those of WT littermates, evidenced by larger and more regenerating myofibers, reduced adipocyte infiltration (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A; third row), hallmarks of human sarcopenia (Taaffe et al., 2009).
evidence: Based on H&E staining shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and citation to Taaffe et al., 2009

claim: Aged MCK-N1ICD mice achieved a higher maximum speed and longer running distance in the treadmill test.
source: Moreover, the aged MCK-N1ICD mice achieved a higher maximum speed and longer running distance in the treadmill test (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: Based on treadmill test data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2E

claim: N1ICD-mdx mice showed upregulation of Hes1 expression in the muscles, indicating Notch activation.
source: To achieve this goal, we generated MCK-N1ICD-mdx mice (short as N1ICD-mdx) and detected upregulation of Hes1 expression in the muscles of the N1ICD-mdx mice (Figure 4A), indicating Notch activation.
evidence: Based on Western blot data shown in Figure 4A

claim: Adult N1ICD-mdx mice showed 11% less body weight and 27% less muscle mass compared with littermate mdx mice.
source: Interestingly, compared with littermate mdx mice, adult N1ICD-mdx mice showed 11% less body weight and 27% less muscle mass (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: Based on body weight and muscle mass measurements shown in Figure 4B and C

claim: N1ICD-mdx mice showed relatively smaller fiber size, but fewer centronuclear and necrotic IgG+ myofibers compared with mdx mice.
source: Consistently, H&E and immunostaining revealed the relatively smaller fiber size, but fewer centronuclear and necrotic IgG+ myofibers in N1ICD-mdx mice, compared with mdx mice (Figure 4D; first row, E and F).
evidence: Based on H&E staining and immunostaining data shown in Figure 4D, E, and F

claim: The muscles of N1ICD-mdx mice showed much less EBD uptake than mdx muscles.
source: In addition, we performed CTX-induced muscle damage, followed by Evans blue dye (EBD) injection to label myofibers with dysfunctional and permeable membranes. Notably, the muscles of N1ICD-mdx mice showed much less EBD uptake than mdx muscles (Figure 4G).
evidence: Based on EBD uptake data shown in Figure 4G

claim: There were fewer EBD+ myofibers in N1ICD-mdx than mdx muscles.
source: Consistently, there were fewer EBD+myofibers in N1ICD-mdx than mdx muscles (Figure 4H).
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4H

claim: H&E staining revealed better muscle regeneration in CTX-injected TA muscles of N1ICD-mdx mice, characterized by more and larger myofibers, and less inflammatory infiltration.
source: H&E staining revealed better muscle regeneration, characterized by more and larger myofibers, and less inflammatory infiltration in the CTX-injected TA muscles of N1ICD-mdx mice (Figure 4D; second row).
evidence: Based on H&E staining shown in Figure 4D

claim: Adult N1ICD-mdx mice exhibited better muscle exercise performance and stronger gripping strength than their littermate mdx mice.
source: Furthermore, adult N1ICD-mdx mice also exhibited better muscle exercise performance and stronger gripping strength than their littermate mdx mice (Figure 4I–K).
evidence: Based on treadmill and gripping strength data shown in Figure 4I–K

claim: Among the total 882 differentially expressed genes, 505 genes were downregulated and 377 genes were upregulated in N1ICD-mdx, compared with mdx muscles.
source: Among the total 882 differentially expressed genes (by ≥1.5–fold), 505 genes were downregulated and 377 genes were upregulated in N1ICD-mdx, compared with mdx muscles (Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: Based on microarray analysis results

claim: Gdf11 was identified as the highest upregulated gene in MCK-N1ICD muscles from the microarray.
source: From the microarray, we identified Gdf11 (Growth Differentiation Factor 11) as the highest upregulated gene in MCK-N1ICD muscles (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Based on microarray data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A

claim: Upregulation of Gdf11 expression was validated in all muscles examined in both MCK-N1ICD-mdx and MLC-N1ICD mice, compared with their littermate controls.
source: Consistently, we validated upregulation of Gdf11 expression in all muscles examined in both MCK-N1ICD-mdx and MLC-N1ICD mice, compared with their littermate controls (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: Based on gene expression validation data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and C

claim: GSEA predicted significant overall enrichment for the downregulated N1ICD-mdx gene-set with human genes that were upregulated in DMD versus healthy human subjects.
source: Strikingly, GSEA predicted significant overall enrichment (false discovery rate q-value = 0.02; familywise-error rate p-value = 0.009) for the downregulated N1ICD-mdx gene-set with human genes that were upregulated in DMD versus healthy human subjects (score, –1.40) (Figure 5B).
evidence: Based on GSEA analysis results shown in Figure 5B

claim: There is a strong trend that N1ICD-mdx upregulated genes were also positively correlated to genes that were expressed at higher levels in healthy human muscles.
source: Similarly, there is a strong trend that N1ICD-mdx upregulated genes were also positively correlated to genes that were expressed at higher levels in healthy human muscles (score = 1.08, q = 0.26, p = 0.13) (Figure 5C).
evidence: Based on GSEA analysis results shown in Figure 5C

claim: N1ICD-mdx muscles expressed higher levels of mature muscle specific Myh1 (MHC-2x), and lower levels of regenerating muscle specific Myh8.
source: Consistent with their reduced degeneration, N1ICD-mdx muscles expressed higher levels of mature muscle specific Myh1 (MHC-2x), and lower levels of regenerating muscle specific Myh8 (Figure 5D).
evidence: Based on heatmap data shown in Figure 5D

claim: Expression of Spp1, the biomarker of human DMD, is significantly lower in N1ICD-mdx muscles, than in mdx muscles.
source: Strikingly, expression of Spp1, the biomarker of human DMD (Pegoraro et al., 2011), is also significantly lower in N1ICD-mdx muscles, than in mdx muscles (Figure 5D).
evidence: Based on heatmap data shown in Figure 5D and citation to Pegoraro et al., 2011

claim: The cell cycle inhibitor p21 (encoded by gene Cdkn1a) and the muscle hypertrophy gene Junb were significantly downregulated in N1ICD-mdx muscles and normal human muscles, compared with corresponding dystrophic muscles.
source: Interestingly, the cell cycle inhibitor p21 (encoded by gene Cdkn1a), a critical modulator of senescence, and the muscle hypertrophy gene Junb (Raffaello et al., 2010) were significantly downregulated in N1ICD-mdx muscles and normal human muscles, compared with corresponding dystrophic muscles (Figure 5D).
evidence: Based on heatmap data shown in Figure 5D and citation to Raffaello et al., 2010

claim: Both N1ICD-mdx and healthy human muscle showed upregulation of Mfn2 (Mitofusin 2), which is involved in mitochondrial fusion, and associated with better muscle glucose metabolism and amelioration of muscle atrophy.
source: Both N1ICD-mdx and healthy human muscle showed upregulation of Mfn2 (Mitofusin 2) (Figure 5D), which is involved in mitochondrial fusion, and associated with better muscle glucose metabolism and amelioration of muscle atrophy (Chen et al., 2010; Sebastian et al., 2012).
evidence: Based on heatmap data shown in Figure 5D and citations to Chen et al., 2010 and Sebastian et al., 2012

claim: Vegfa was upregulated in N1ICD-mdx samples, which stimulates angiogenesis and improves vascular function.
source: In addition, upregulated in N1ICD-mdx samples was Vegfa (Figure 5D), which stimulates angiogenesis and improves vascular function.
evidence: Based on heatmap data shown in Figure 5D and established knowledge about Vegfa function

claim: Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA) of commonly up- and down-regulated genes predicted significantly elevated 'vasculogenesis', and decreased 'fibrosis' in N1ICD-mdx muscles.
source: Consistently, Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA) of commonly up- and down-regulated genes predicted significantly elevated 'vasculogenesis', and decreased 'fibrosis' in N1ICD-mdx muscles (Figure 5E).
evidence: Based on IPA analysis results shown in Figure 5E

claim: Notch target genes Hey2, Hes5 and Nrarp were upregulated in N1ICD-mdx muscles, confirming Notch activation.
source: Notch target genes Hey2, Hes5 and Nrarp were upregulated in N1ICD-mdx muscles (Figure 5F), confirming Notch activation.
evidence: Based on heatmap data shown in Figure 5F

claim: Dysferlin (dysf) and α-dystrobrevin (Dtna), two components of dystrophin-glycoprotein complex essential for sarcolemma repair and neuromuscular junction maturation, were significantly elevated in N1ICD-mdx muscles.
source: Interestingly, dysferlin (dysf) and α-dystrobrevin (Dtna), two components of dystrophin-glycoprotein complex essential for sarcolemma repair and neuromuscular junction maturation (Bansal et al., 2003; Grady et al., 1999), were significantly elevated in N1ICD-mdx muscles (Figure 5F).
evidence: Based on heatmap data shown in Figure 5F and citations to Bansal et al., 2003 and Grady et al., 1999

claim: A panel of stem cell senescence modulators, p21 (Cdkn1a), p27 (Cdkn1b) and Rbl1 were all significantly downregulated in N1ICD-mdx muscles.
source: Furthermore, a panel of stem cell senescence modulators, p21 (Cdkn1a), p27 (Cdkn1b) and Rbl1 (Cheung and Rando, 2013; Narita et al., 2003; Sousa-Victor et al., 2014) were all significantly downregulated in N1ICD-mdx muscles (Figure 5F).
evidence: Based on heatmap data shown in Figure 5F and citations to Cheung and Rando, 2013; Narita et al., 2003; Sousa-Victor et al., 2014

claim: CTX-damaged 17-month old MCK-N1ICD muscles, and adult N1ICD-mdx muscles showed more Pax7+ SCs.
source: Consistent with improved muscle regeneration, CTX-damaged 17-month old MCK-N1ICD muscles, and adult N1ICD-mdx muscles showed more Pax7+ SCs (Figure 6A–C), and elevated expression of Pax7 than did mdx muscles (Figure 6D).
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence and Western blot data shown in Figure 6A–D

claim: No Pax7+/Td+ cells were detected in EDL myofibers from MCK-N1ICD mice.
source: To exclude the possibility that dedifferentiation of MCK-Cre+ myocytes contribute to the increases of SCs, we again performed lineage tracing using MCK-Cre in combination with N1ICD and Td reporter mice. Staining of the EDL myofiber with Pax7 antibody didn't detect any Pax7+/Td+ cells (Figure 6E).
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6E

claim: The increase of SCs number in MCK-N1ICD mice is not a result of myocyte dedifferentiation.
source: Therefore, unlike the MLC-N1ICD mice, the increase of SCs number in MCK-N1ICD mice is not a result of myocyte dedifferentiation.
evidence: Based on the lineage tracing data showing no Pax7+/Td+ cells

claim: In skeletal muscle of N1ICD-mdx mice, elevated expression of two Notch ligands, Jag2 and Dll4, was detected compared with mdx muscles.
source: In skeletal muscle of N1ICD-mdx mice, we detected elevated expression of two Notch ligands, Jag2 and Dll4, compared with mdx muscles (Figure 6F).
evidence: Based on gene expression data shown in Figure 6F

claim: Immunostaining of EDL myofibers revealed stronger Dll4 immunofluorescence in MCK-N1ICD than in WT myofibers.
source: Consistently, immunostaining of EDL myofibers revealed stronger Dll4 immunofluorescence in MCK-N1ICD than in WT myofibers (Figure 6G and H).
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6G and H

claim: 41% SCs were GFP+/Pax7+ in MCK-N1ICD-CpGFP mice, compared with 26% GFP+/Pax7+ SCs in control CpGFP mice.
source: Immunostaining of EDL myofibers with Pax7 and GFP antibodies revealed that 41% SCs were GFP+/Pax7+ in MCK-N1ICD-CpGFP mice, compared with 26% GFP+/Pax7+ SCs in control CpGFP mice (Figure 6I and J).
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence and quantification data shown in Figure 6I and J

claim: Stronger GFP fluorescence was observed in myofibers of MCK-N1ICD-CpGFP mice, compared with those of CpGFP mice, confirming Notch activation by N1ICD OE.
source: As a positive control, we observed stronger GFP fluorescence in myofibers of MCK-N1ICD-CpGFP mice, compared with those of CpGFP mice (Figure 6I and K), confirming Notch activation by N1ICD OE.
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6I and K

claim: Expression of Notch1 and its target gene Hes1, as well as Notch ligand Dll4 and Jag2 were detected in trypsin-stripped myofibers, though at lower levels compared to the non-trypsin-stripped myofibers.
source: Notably, expression of Notch1 and its target gene Hes1, as well as Notch ligand Dll4 and Jag2 were detected in these trypsin-stripped myofibers, though at lower levels compared to the non-trypsin-stripped myofibers (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C—E).
evidence: Based on RT-PCR and Western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2C—E

claim: N1ICD-mdx mice treated with DMSO ran faster and farther than their littermate mdx mice, but after DBZ treatment both genotypes showed similar maximum speed and distance in the treadmill test.
source: Whereas the N1ICD-mdx mice treated with DMSO ran faster and farther than their littermate mdx mice, after DBZ treatment both genotypes showed similar maximum speed and distance in the treadmill test (Figure 7B and C).
evidence: Based on treadmill test data shown in Figure 7B and C

claim: DBZ-treated N1ICD-mdx muscle displayed similar EBD uptake levels to the mdx mice, indicating similar extent of muscle repair.
source: In addition, DBZ-treated N1ICD-mdx muscle displayed similar EBD uptake levels to the mdx mice, indicating similar extent of muscle repair (Figure 7D).
evidence: Based on EBD uptake data shown in Figure 7D

claim: H&E staining revealed better muscle regeneration in N1ICD-mdx than mdx mice in DMSO group, and DBZ administration rendered the regeneration similarly poor in both N1ICD-mdx and mdx mice.
source: Indeed, H&E staining revealed better muscle regeneration in N1ICD-mdx than mdx mice in DMSO group, and DBZ administration rendered the regeneration similarly poor in both N1ICD-mdx and mdx mice (Figure 7E).
evidence: Based on H&E staining data shown in Figure 7E

claim: The amelioration of muscle atrophy and dysfunction in N1ICD-mdx mice is mediated by modulation of Notch signaling in SCs.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrate that the amelioration of muscle atrophy and dysfunction in N1ICD-mdx mice is mediated by modulation of Notch signaling in SCs.
evidence: Based on the DBZ treatment experiments showing that blocking Notch signaling abolishes the improvements

claim: N1ICD overexpression in committed and activated SCs, induced by Myf5Cre and Myod1Cre, respectively, completely blocked the embryonic muscle development.
source: Collectively, our study demonstrates stage-specific functions of Notch during myogenesis. We show that N1ICD overexpression in committed and activated SCs, induced by Myf5Cre and Myod1Cre, respectively, completely blocked the embryonic muscle development (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A) (Mourikis et al., 2012a).
evidence: Based on H&E staining shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A and citation to Mourikis et al., 2012a

claim: Myod1Cre-N1ICD mice failed to survive to birth, and showed total absence of MyoD and MyoG expression.
source: Myod1Cre-N1ICD mice failed to survive to birth, and showed total absence of MyoD and MyoG expression (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: Based on immunostaining data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B and C

claim: MLC-N1ICD mice had relatively normal embryonic muscle development evidenced by similar body weight and muscle morphology at birth, but exhibited defective postnatal muscle growth and regeneration.
source: However, MLC-N1ICD mice had relatively normal embryonic muscle development evidenced by similar body weight and muscle morphology at birth, but exhibited defective postnatal muscle growth and regeneration (Figure 8).
evidence: Based on the combined experimental data and summary diagram in Figure 8

claim: Adult MCK-N1ICD mice had normal muscle growth, and better muscle regeneration and motor function as they age.
source: Furthermore, adult MCK-N1ICD mice had normal muscle growth, and better muscle regeneration and motor function as they age (Figure 8).
evidence: Based on the combined experimental data and summary diagram in Figure 8

claim: MCK-N1ICD boosted muscle function and regenerative capacity in mdx mice.
source: More importantly, MCK-N1ICD boosted muscle function and regenerative capacity in mdx mice (Figure 8).
evidence: Based on the combined experimental data and summary diagram in Figure 8

claim: Notch-induced dedifferentiation is restricted to mononucleated myocytes, which doesn't require cytokinesis as for multinucleated myofibers.
source: Intriguingly, dedifferentiation was only observed in a portion of MLC-N1ICD cells, despite that N1ICD was overexpressed in both pre-fusion myocytes and post-fusion myotubes. By contrast, dedifferentiation was not observed in MCK-N1ICD mice, which specifically overexpress N1ICD in myotubes. Based on these comparisons, we concluded that Notch-induced dedifferentiation is restricted to mononucleated myocytes, which doesn't require cytokinesis as for multinucleated myofibers.
evidence: Based on comparison of MLC-N1ICD and MCK-N1ICD phenotypes

claim: Activation of Notch1 in myotubes improved motor function and muscle regeneration of both aged and mdx mice.
source: Activation of Notch1 in myotubes improved motor function and muscle regeneration of both aged and mdx mice.
evidence: Based on the combined experimental data from MCK-N1ICD mice

claim: Activation of Notch1 in myotubes was accompanied by upregulation of Dll/Jag ligand expression in myofibers, higher Notch activity in juxtaposed SCs, as well as greater regenerative potentials of SCs in MCK-N1ICD mice.
source: This is accompanied by upregulation of Dll/Jag ligand expression in myofibers, higher Notch activity in juxtaposed SCs, as well as greater regenerative potentials of SCs in MCK-N1ICD mice.
evidence: Based on the combined experimental data showing ligand expression, Notch reporter activity, and SC numbers

claim: Notch signaling deficiency in SCs is a prominent feature of aged and dystrophic muscles.
source: Consistently, Notch signaling deficiency in SCs is a prominent feature of aged and dystrophic muscles (Conboy et al., 2003; Jiang et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Conboy et al., 2003 and Jiang et al., 2014

claim: Dll/Jag ligands on intact myofibers should only activate Notch signaling in the SCs, but not the other cells that are prevented from direct physical interaction with the myofiber by the basal lamina.
source: As SCs are the only cells that are directly attached to the myofibers, Dll/Jag ligands on intact myofibers should only activate Notch signaling in the SCs, but not the other cells (for example blood vessel-associated cells and interstitial cells) that are prevented from direct physical interaction with the myofiber by the basal lamina.
evidence: Based on anatomical knowledge and logical inference

claim: The normalizing effects of DBZ on the improved muscle function in the MCK-N1ICD mice demonstrates that Notch-dependent enhancement of SCs' regenerative potential is the underlying molecular and cellular mechanism mediating the effect of N1ICD overexpression in myofibers.
source: Thus, the normalizing effects of DBZ on the improved muscle function in the MCK-N1ICD mice demonstrates that Notch-dependent enhancement of SCs' regenerative potential is the underlying molecular and cellular mechanism mediating the effect of N1ICD overexpression in myofibers.
evidence: Based on the DBZ treatment experiments and logical inference

claim: Activation of Notch1 improves myotube's function as a stem cell niche.
source: Most importantly, our study demonstrates that activation of Notch1 improves myotube's function as a stem cell niche.
evidence: Based on the combined experimental data showing improved SC function in MCK-N1ICD mice

claim: One strategy to ameliorate sarcopenia and muscle dystrophy diseases is through modulating Notch signaling in the myofiber.
source: This finding suggests that one strategy to ameliorate sarcopenia and muscle dystrophy diseases is through modulating Notch signaling in the myofiber.
evidence: Based on the therapeutic implications of the MCK-N1ICD results

claim: Constitutive Notch1 activation dedifferentiates myocytes into Pax7 quiescent satellite cells, leading to severe defects in muscle growth and regeneration, and postnatal lethality.
source: Specifically, constitutive Notch1 activation dedifferentiates myocytes into Pax7 quiescent satellite cells, leading to severe defects in muscle growth and regeneration, and postnatal lethality.
evidence: Based on the combined experimental data from MLC-N1ICD mice

claim: Myotube-specific Notch1 activation improves the regeneration and exercise performance of aged and dystrophic muscles.
source: By contrast, myotube-specific Notch1 activation improves the regeneration and exercise performance of aged and dystrophic muscles.
evidence: Based on the combined experimental data from MCK-N1ICD mice

claim: Notch1 activation in myotubes upregulates the expression of Notch ligands, which modulate Notch signaling in the adjacent satellite cells to enhance their regenerative capacity.
source: Mechanistically, Notch1 activation in myotubes upregulates the expression of Notch ligands, which modulate Notch signaling in the adjacent satellite cells to enhance their regenerative capacity.
evidence: Based on the combined experimental data showing ligand upregulation, increased Notch activity in SCs, and improved regeneration

claim: Notch1 activity improves myotube's function as a stem cell niche.
source: These results highlight context-dependent effects of Notch activation during myogenesis, and demonstrate that Notch1 activity improves myotube's function as a stem cell niche.
evidence: Based on the combined experimental data from MCK-N1ICD mice

claim: Higher Jag1 expression is associated with better muscle phenotypes of dystrophic mice and dogs.
source: Genetic mapping studies showed that the higher Jag1 expression is associated with better muscle phenotypes of dystrophic mice and dogs (Vieira et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Vieira et al., 2015

claim: Jag1 overexpression rescued the muscular dystrophy phenotype of dystrophin-deficient zebrafish.
source: Notably, Jag1 overexpression rescued the muscular dystrophy phenotype of dystrophin-deficient zebrafish (Vieira et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Vieira et al., 2015
